name: GAIN: universal salt iodization (Founders Pledge)
summary: Universal salt iodization, which the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN) supports with governments and salt producers. Founders Pledge's recreation of GiveWell's 2014 model, with moral weights updated in 2021, covers GAIN and ICCIDD (now Iodine Global Network) together: iodine in childhood raises IQ and later earnings. Founders Pledge's GAIN page gives no cost-effectiveness figure of its own; this is its shared salt-iodization sheet, whose impact row names GAIN/ICCIDD, so GAIN's and IGN's models are the same analysis: don't add them up.

source.title: Founders Pledge salt iodization CEA (recreated GiveWell 2014 model), applied to its GAIN universal salt iodization recommendation

sections.title: Per dollar
sections.explainer: charityevals' step: Founders Pledge's units of value per $100,000, per dollar.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not Founders Pledge's. With credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as their contribution, and they get their share of the outcome.

rows.label: Discount rate
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate (Your values). Founders Pledge uses 4%, from GiveWell's 2020 cost-effectiveness analysis (Iodine!B3); the evaluator view pins it there.

rows.label: Duration of long-term benefits (years)

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: How many working years the earnings gain lasts. FP takes GiveWell's 2020 duration for deworming's long-term benefits (40) and uses it for iodine too. The range is GiveWell's 2014 one from the sheet's parameters tab (10 to 40 years; its 2014 best guess was 25).

rows.label: Cost per person per year

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: Cost of iodizing salt per person covered per year: $0.10 for small salt plants (Horton, Mannar and Wesley 2008, Table 1). The low end, $0.05, is their figure for large producers; $0.08 is GiveWell's average. GAIN's own estimate, quoted on Founders Pledge's GAIN page, is $0.05 to $0.18 per person given access to iodized salt, in India, Ethiopia, Bangladesh and the Philippines; the sheet uses the per-year cost above.

rows.label: Internal validity (replicability)

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: How far the trials' effect on IQ is likely to replicate. Higher than for deworming because there are six RCTs. Range from GiveWell's pessimistic and optimistic cases.

rows.label: External validity

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: The trials were run where deficiency was moderate. GiveWell's 70% rests on ICCIDD's likely countries having mild or no deficiency and on real-world programs in ICCIDD/GAIN countries doing worse than trials (the sheet's note, Parameters G49); Founders Pledge applies the same figure to GAIN.

rows.label: Leverage (dollars of impact per dollar spent)

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: 1 = no leverage. GiveWell assumes none: GAIN spends about $0.08 per additional person iodized, about the full cost of iodization (the sheet's note, Parameters G50). The optimistic case, 2, assumes governments spend more because of it.

rows.label: Share of iodine's benefit that lasts into adulthood

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: Whether the IQ gain persists: trials with long follow-ups are few, and IQ gains from early-childhood programs often fade.

rows.label: Household coverage achieved

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: A national campaign won't reach every household (some don't buy salt, some producers don't iodize, remote areas). The cost per person is per head of the whole population, so the benefit is scaled down instead.

rows.label: Probability that GAIN/ICCIDD (now IGN) has an impact

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: GiveWell had not seen compelling evidence that iodization rose because of GAIN's or ICCIDD's (now IGN's) work, so it gives even odds. Founders Pledge's sheet asks this of GAIN and ICCIDD together and doesn't separate them, so GAIN's model is the same as IGN's. This is the evaluator's own counterfactual credit and applies in both views. Founders Pledge's 2022 GAIN page cites Bangladesh and Vietnam as evidence that GAIN's impact is likelier than GiveWell thought, but the sheet keeps GiveWell's 0.5.

rows.label: Share of children who benefit

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: Allows for the chance that a higher IQ doesn't raise wellbeing for everyone in very poor settings. The low case follows deworming (only wage earners and a few others gain).

rows.label: Equivalent increase in wages from iodine throughout childhood

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: Iodine raises IQ by about 0.25 SD (about 4 points); GiveWell turns that into a wage gain of about 3.6% from estimates of the IQ–wage link (DCP2, Zax and Rees 2002).

rows.label: Years of childhood (for iodine)

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: By definition: children under 15.

rows.label: Share of the population under 15

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: World Bank, population aged 0–14, Sub-Saharan Africa, 2014.

rows.label: Benefit on one year's income, discounted 10 years (ln income)
rows.explainer: The yearly gain in ln(income) for a worker who had iodine throughout childhood, discounted back 10 years for the wait between childhood and work.

rows.label: Present value of lifetime benefits per worker (ln income)
rows.explainer: The sheet's =PV(rate, 40, -gain, 0, 1): 40 years of the gain, paid at the start of each year, discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Present value of lifetime benefits per worker, after validity adjustments
Benefit per person per year of iodization, adjusted for coverage and age (ln income)
rows.explainer: One year of iodized salt gives a child one fifteenth of a childhood's benefit; children under 15 are 43% of the people covered.

rows.label: Increase in ln(consumption) per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources on, leverage is dropped (any government money it draws in is a contributor's own share); FP's leverage is 1 anyway, so nothing changes at the defaults. The cost per person is already the full cost of iodization, whoever pays it.

rows.label: Increase in ln(consumption) per $100,000
Value of increasing ln(consumption) by one unit for one person for one year
rows.explainer: GiveWell's weight on income (1/ln 2 = 1.4427, so that doubling income for a year is worth 1). FP rounds it to 1.44 (Iodine!B30, GiveWell's 2020 CEA); the evaluator view pins that.

rows.label: Units of value per $100,000 to salt iodization
Units of value per $100,000 to GiveDirectly (GiveWell 2020)

source.title: Founders Pledge, salt iodization CEA (recreated from GiveWell's 2014 model; moral weights updated February 2021)

rows.explainer: GiveWell's 2020 value for cash transfers, used only for FP's comparison below.

rows.label: Salt iodization vs cash (multiple of GiveDirectly)
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's headline: about 7 times as cost-effective as GiveDirectly. Not used for our result, which goes from the units of value directly.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: Founders Pledge's result per dollar instead of per $100,000. Its units are GiveWell's: one unit is a year of doubled consumption for one person.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this grant's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per donor dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
